<!-- head-1: body_md -->
The parameter $p$ counts all quadrature nodes in the present paper. In \cite{Kuznetsov_2026}, it counts only the nodes in the fourth quadrant: the complete quadrature rule has $2p+1$ nodes, consisting of those nodes, their negatives, and the origin. If the construction is formally extended to the principal character $\chi_0$ modulo $1$, then the corresponding weights here are one half of those in \cite{Kuznetsov_2026}, while the nodes and interpolation points agree. With this normalization, $\zeta_p(s)=L_{2p+1}(s,\chi_0)$ (though this formal comparison lies outside the standing assumption $q\ge3$).
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop_symmetry}
${}$ \begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For all $0\le r<q$
\begin{equation}\label{K_symmetry_1}
K_{\chi,q-1-r}(-x)=\chi(-1) K_{\chi,r}(x), \;\;\; x\in {\mathbb R}. 
\end{equation}
\item[(ii)]
 When $4|q$, we have for all $0\le r < q/2$
\begin{equation}\label{K_symmetry_2}
K_{\chi,r+q/2}(x)={\textnormal i} (-1)^r  K_{\chi,r}(x), \;\;\; x\in {\mathbb R}. 
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The definition \eqref{def_W_chi} gives the quasiperiodicity and parity identities
\begin{equation*}
W_{\chi}(u+q)=(-1)^q W_{\chi}(u), \;\;\;
W_{\chi}(-u)=-\chi(-1) W_{\chi}(u). 
\end{equation*}
Substituting these identities into \eqref{def_K_chi_r} proves \eqref{K_symmetry_1}. To prove \eqref{K_symmetry_2}, suppose that $4|q$. Then $\chi(1+q/2)=-1$; otherwise, $\chi$ would factor through modulus $q/2$, contradicting its primitivity.  Every $n$ coprime to $q$ is odd, and hence
\[
n+\frac{q}{2} \equiv n \Big(1+\frac{q}{2} \Big) 
\; (\textnormal{mod} \; q). 
\]
It follows that $\chi(n+q/2)=-\chi(n)$ for every integer $n$, including those not coprime to $q$, for which both sides vanish. Shifting the summation index in \eqref{def_W_chi} by $q/2$ then yields
\[
W_{\chi}\Big(u+\frac{q}{2}\Big)=e^{-\frac{\pi {\textnormal i} q}{4}} W_{\chi}(u).
\] 
Combining this identity with \eqref{def_K_chi_r} gives  \eqref{K_symmetry_2}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
